comparison: Perfect agreement on lineage tracing claims (C61-C66). Both evaluations support that acinar cells are the cell-of-origin and that conversion occurs without proliferation. OpenEval finds the methodology rigorous; peer reviewers raise no concerns about these findings.

Perfect agreement on temporal analysis claims (C78-C82). Both evaluations support the sequential two-step model of reprogramming. OpenEval considers this a key conceptual advance; peer reviewers do not challenge the temporal data, though they request more developmental context.

Perfect agreement on fate suppression claims (C83-C86). Both evaluations support that Mafa and Pdx1 suppress δ-cell fate in a dose-dependent manner. OpenEval finds the data supports the suppression model; peer reviewers do not challenge these findings.

Perfect agreement on the integrative model claims (C87-C96). Both evaluations support the overall conceptual framework. OpenEval finds the model well-supported by cumulative evidence; peer reviewers describe results as 'very interesting and overall convincing' despite some methodological concerns about specific assays.

Significant disagreement on δ-cell characterization (C9-C16, C37). OpenEval finds multiple complementary methods provide strong evidence for δ-cell identity (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers raise serious concerns about hormone secretion assays and FACS purification, noting induced δ-cells don't produce more somatostatin than islet controls despite islets being only 5% δ-cells (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on α-cell characterization (C38-C41, C45-C51, C58). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence support α-cell identity, though mechanism for optimal virus ratio remains speculative (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question co-infection efficiency and raise FACS purification concerns about potential autofluorescence artifacts (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on gene profiling for δ-cells (C17-C22). OpenEval finds the gene profiling data and analysis appropriately account for δ-cells being a minor islet population (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers' concerns about FACS purification and hormone secretion create uncertainty about the overall δ-cell characterization including gene profiling (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on methylation analysis for δ-cells (C26-C31). OpenEval finds bisulfite sequencing demonstrates appropriate methylation changes and is methodologically sound (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers' broader concerns about FACS purification undermine confidence in the methylation data derived from purified cells (UNCERTAIN).

Significant disagreement on functional secretion for δ-cells (C34-C36). OpenEval finds radioimmunoassay data demonstrates hormone secretion and supports functional competence (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers specifically challenge this, noting induced δ-cells don't produce more somatostatin than islet controls despite islets containing only 5% δ-cells, questioning the 'cellular machineries' claim (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on α-cell functional and epigenetic data (C52-C57). OpenEval finds functional secretion and DNA methylation analysis support α-cell identity, with incomplete reprogramming appropriately acknowledged (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question co-infection efficiency and FACS purification, creating uncertainty about α-cell characterization (UNCERTAIN).

Agreement on transcription factor hierarchy (C70, C73-C74). Both evaluations support that Ngn3 uniquely establishes a generic endocrine state. OpenEval considers this a key mechanistic insight (SUPPORTED); peer reviewers don't challenge the findings but request more discussion about developmental relevance (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on acinar factor blocking (C75-C77). Both evaluations support that acinar factors block reprogramming and must be down-regulated. OpenEval finds this an important mechanistic finding (SUPPORTED); peer reviewers don't challenge the data but request developmental context (SUPPORTED).

Disagreement on Ngn3+Pdx1 combination effects (C3, C5). OpenEval finds the data support that this combination produces insulin-positive cells (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question why no hormone-positive cells appear if infection rates are <100%, finding this 'quite surprising' and suggesting methodological issues (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on transient expression claim (C8). OpenEval finds the data support transient expression of reprogramming factors (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question transgene silencing stability and timeframe, asking for confirmation that exogenous transgenes are silenced, creating uncertainty (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on long-term persistence of δ-cells (C12). OpenEval finds persistence over time supports δ-cell identity (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question whether 2 months is sufficient to establish stability, asking 'is this the end?' given cells are not in the right islet environment (UNCERTAIN).

Disagreement on long-term persistence of α-cells (C47). OpenEval finds persistence supports α-cell identity (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers question long-term stability beyond 2 months, asking whether cells are stable given they're not in the right islet environment (UNCERTAIN).

Agreement on distinction from developmental progenitors (C104-C105). Both evaluations support that induced endocrine state differs from developmental progenitors and that progenitor markers are absent. OpenEval notes this is appropriately acknowledged (SUPPORTED); peer reviewers acknowledge the distinction and request more discussion on similarities/differences (SUPPORTED).

Agreement on developmental comparison context (C97, C102-C103). Both evaluations support the comparison between developmental and reprogramming contexts. OpenEval finds the comparison well-supported by citations and acknowledgment of different epigenetic contexts (SUPPORTED); peer reviewers request more discussion but don't challenge the claims (SUPPORTED).

Both address methylation analysis (C25), but different aspects. OpenEval evaluates the somatostatin promoter methylation as a useful negative control (SUPPORTED). Peer reviewers' concerns about FACS purification affect confidence in methylation data generally (UNCERTAIN), though they don't specifically address the somatostatin promoter finding.

Both address co-infection efficiency issues (C107-C112 for OpenEval; C40-C41 overlap with peer concerns). OpenEval acknowledges the mechanistic explanation for optimal virus ratio is speculative (UNCERTAIN). Peer reviewers question co-infection efficiency more broadly, noting contradictions in the data about whether 100% co-infection is required (UNCERTAIN).

OpenEval evaluates background claims about prior β-cell induction work (C1, C59-C60, C120) as appropriately cited and supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge claims in pancreatic biology (C6, C10, C42-C44, C67-C69, C71-C72, C106, C115-C117) as appropriately cited context. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these background knowledge claims.

OpenEval evaluates broader cell reprogramming field context claims (C32-C33, C113-C114) as appropriately cited and reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these conceptual framework claims.
